title: The Cancer Genome Atlas: Creating Lasting Value beyond Its Data
note: The overview of the TCGA Pan-Cancer Atlas, which describes what the project produced and how the data are shared.

title: Cell-of-Origin Patterns Dominate the Molecular Classification of 10,000 Tumors from 33 Types of Cancer
authors: Hoadley KA, Yau C, Hinoue T, et al. (The Cancer Genome Atlas Research Network)
note: The gene expression, copy number, microRNA and molecular subtype data of this database come from this paper.

title: An Integrated TCGA Pan-Cancer Clinical Data Resource to Drive High-Quality Survival Outcome Analytics
authors: Liu J, Lichtenberg T, Hoadley KA, et al. (The Cancer Genome Atlas Research Network)
note: The clinical outcome data (survival times and events) of this database come from this paper.

title: The Immune Landscape of Cancer
authors: Thorsson V, Gibbs DL, Brown SD, et al. (The Cancer Genome Atlas Research Network)
note: The immune signature scores, immune subtypes and viral read counts of this database come from this paper.

title: Scalable Open Science Approach for Mutation Calling of Tumor Exomes Using Multiple Genomic Pipelines
authors: Ellrott K, Bailey MH, Saksena G, et al. (The Cancer Genome Atlas Research Network)
note: The mutation calls (the MC3 call set) and the tumor mutation burden of this database come from this paper.

title: Genomic and Molecular Landscape of DNA Damage Repair Deficiency across The Cancer Genome Atlas
authors: Knijnenburg TA, Wang L, Zimmermann MT, et al. (The Cancer Genome Atlas Research Network)
note: The homologous recombination deficiency and microsatellite instability scores of this database come from this paper.

title: Oncogenic Signaling Pathways in The Cancer Genome Atlas
authors: Sanchez-Vega F, Mina M, Armenia J, et al. (The Cancer Genome Atlas Research Network)
note: Describes the cancer signaling pathways that are altered in these tumors, used for pathway-level annotations.

title: Comprehensive Characterization of Cancer Driver Genes and Mutations
authors: Bailey MH, Tokheim C, Porta-Pardo E, et al. (The Cancer Genome Atlas Research Network)
note: Describes the driver genes and mutations identified across these tumors.

title: The Cancer Genome Atlas Pan-Cancer analysis project
authors: Weinstein JN, Collisson EA, Mills GB, et al. (The Cancer Genome Atlas Research Network)
note: The original description of the TCGA Pan-Cancer project.

title: GISTIC2.0 facilitates sensitive and confident localization of the targets of focal somatic copy-number alteration in human cancers
authors: Mermel CH, Schumacher SE, Hill B, et al.
note: The method (GISTIC2.0) behind the copy number classes: it finds the regions of the genome that are gained or lost in tumors.

title: A pan-cancer proteomic perspective on The Cancer Genome Atlas
authors: Akbani R, Ng PK, Werner HM, et al.
note: The protein measurements (reverse-phase protein arrays) of this database are described in this paper.

title: Multiplatform analysis of 12 cancer types reveals molecular classification within and across tissues of origin
authors: Hoadley KA, Yau C, Wolf DM, et al.
note: The method behind the gene programs (molecular groupings) used in this database.

title: Inference of transcriptional regulation in cancers
authors: Jiang P, Freedman ML, Liu JS, et al.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
note: The method (RABIT) that estimates how active each transcription factor, a protein that switches genes on or off, is in each tumor.

title: Inferring tumour purity and stromal and immune cell admixture from expression data
authors: Yoshihara K, Shahmoradgoli M, Martínez E, et al.
note: The method (ESTIMATE) that scores tumor purity and the amount of stromal and immune cells in a tumor sample from gene expression.

title: Visualizing and interpreting cancer genomics data via the Xena platform
authors: Goldman MJ, Craft B, Hastie M, et al.
note: The data files were downloaded from the UCSC Xena platform described in this paper.

title: The Cancer Genome Atlas Program (TCGA)
authors: National Cancer Institute and National Human Genome Research Institute
note: The program that produced the tumor data in this database.
